az_weavers_needle.blurb: Weavers Needle is a volcanic spire in the Superstition Mountains east of Phoenix, reached on foot from the Peralta Trailhead by way of Fremont Saddle. All five climbs here are trad: one easy line of low-angle terrain, one around 5.7, and three at 5.9. Most routes run three or four pitches. The rock can be poor in places, so test holds, place protection where you can, and wear a helmet. A round trip is about 8 miles with roughly 3,300 feet of gain, so expect most of a day, and the lower trail can be hot at midday even in early November.
az_weavers_needle.approach: Follow the Peralta Canyon Trail from the Peralta Trailhead up to Fremont Saddle and keep going toward the Needle. There is no trail to the west chimney, so leave the main path at a cairn.

az_owl_rock.blurb: Owl Rock is a freestanding rock in the East Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold in southeastern Arizona, near the Ironwood Road turnoff beside Batline, Zappa and Entrance domes. It holds five routes: four trad lines from about 5.5 to 5.9, plus one hard sport route at 5.12 on the overhanging side. The front face carries the area's best-known line, a mixed route graded 5.9. The drive in is dirt, and passenger cars generally manage it unless there has been heavy rain.

az_east_face_area.blurb: East Face Area is a small section of the Mesquite Wash Rockpile, a granite outcrop beside the Beeline Highway (SR 87) in central Arizona. It has five trad routes: a 5.5, a 5.6, and three around 5.10, one of which is marked R. The rockpile's main face points east. There is no established trail, so the walk in follows the highway shoulder south, then a drainage west, and is best done with a light touch on the ground.

az_boulder_and_main_wall_the.blurb: The Boulder and Main Wall sits in the Rattlesnake Pinnacles of West Stronghold, in Cochise Stronghold, southeastern Arizona. It has five trad routes of two to four pitches, mostly 5.9 to 5.10 with one easier 5.8 line. The Boulder has four routes that can each be climbed as a single pitch, and you can downclimb from its top to the Main Wall. The Boulder stays shady for a long time and the Main Wall holds shade until about 1 p.m., so early starts are advised. The approach follows the Whale Dome Drainage and is rough on dogs: allow about 25 minutes if experienced, an hour if new to it.

az_3_checkerboard.blurb: Checkerboard is a small, low-angle, dark-toned cliff in the Chessman Area on Mount Lemmon, near Tucson. Its five routes are a mix of sport and trad, from 5.8 to 5.10, with most at 5.9. The wall stays in shade until about 2 p.m., which suits warm days. The walk up is short but strenuous, with a little scrambling. Climbers coming from the lower fork head up and left, past the neighbouring Queen sector.
az_3_checkerboard.approach: Hike straight up the rocky drainage for about 15 minutes, with a small amount of scrambling. At the fork near the base of the cliff take the uphill left branch, wind through shrubs, and continue left past the Queen sector.
